scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

CL-03.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

H-REQUESTER-FRAMING.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August; building an AI agent that auto-answers tickets and fixes wrong bills will restore baseline.

H-AMI-READ-ISSUE.statement: Missing or delayed AMI register reads from MDMS lead to increased estimation and billing errors, driving dispute surge.

H-FIELD-READ-ISSUE.statement: Contracted field manual read process suffers from staffing shortages or route execution gaps, causing missed reads and estimation errors.

H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE.statement: Recent changes to billing import validation rules introduced incorrect tariff application or read-type handling, generating wrong bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The dispute volume rose sharply starting in August, confirming the surge described in the problem statement.

The observation shows that disputed bills are roughly split between ESTIMATED (1240) and ACTUAL (1785) read types, with a higher count for ACTUAL reads. This indicates that billing errors leading to disputes are not confined to estimation issues but also affect bills based on actual meter reads.
The tariff change log contains no records, indicating no recent tariff or billing import validation rule changes were recorded.

The route completion metric for Aug‑Sep 2026 shows 0.88 completion (9,200 manual read accounts) against a target of 0.95, indicating field manual read execution is below target and may contribute to estimation errors and disputes.

E-05.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The stakeholder reports a shortage of three field readers since July causing delayed routes and estimated bills, indicating a field staffing issue that could drive estimation errors and disputes.

The observation shows that dispute tickets are being responded to within the SLA (median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days against a 3‑day SLA), indicating response performance is not the bottleneck despite high ticket volume.

E-07.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The stakeholder confirms that no tariff or billing rule changes have occurred this year, indicating that recent tariff modifications are not driving the dispute surge.
